text:
Maria: Acme says they're getting a flood of 429s on their dedicated pool starting ~09:10 UTC, high severity. Any oncall available?
Acme-SRE: We applied a quota update through the admin API at 09:10:12 to test lower billing units. Immediately afterwards customers hit 429s. Tenant acme-897a3. Request ids r-7f1, r-7f2 shown in logs.
Maria: can you paste the exact payload you sent and how you called the API?
Acme-SRE: payload from our infra script: 
```
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-897a3",
  "plan": "dedicated-standard",
  "default_units": 6000,
  "quota_scale": "0.001"
}
```
We POSTed to /admin/v1/tenants/acme-897a3/quota with our service account token. Note we serialize floats as strings in our internal templating.
Sam: that stands out. quota_scale should be numeric. There's a legacy path in quota-service that casts with `int()` after `json.loads`; strings that look like floats become 0 when coerced.
Jin (oncall): pulling quota-service logs now. Confirmed at 09:10:14 the effective scale became 0 for acme-897a3. Log: 
```
[09:10:14] quota-service check tenant=acme-897a3 default=6000 received_scale="0.001" parsed_scale=0 effective_units=0
[09:10:14] throttle -> 429 route=/v1/generate request_id=r-7f1
```
Jin (oncall): we reverted the quota object at 09:12:03 which restored traffic by ~09:14.
Maria: thanks. Need repro steps and a rally plan so Support can explain and Product can fix UI/validation.
Sam: repro I used locally: 1) POST the above payload (quota_scale as string) 2) hammer the generate endpoint: `ab -n 80 -c 8 https://api.dedicated.redwood/v1/generate` 3) watch 429s until rollback. Example curl: 
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/tenants/acme-897a3/quota" \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d @payload.json
```
Acme-SRE: confirmed that once the quota object had effective_units==0, all requests were rate-limited irrespective of token or route. Customer verified recovery after rollback.
Priya: proposed fixes: 1) server-side strict validation for quota_scale types (P0) 2) UI guardrails to not accept free-form strings (P1) 3) safety floor: ensure effective_units >= 1 for any dedicated tenant (P0) 4) add an alert that trips when any dedicated tenant's effective_units == 0 (P1)
Sam: also recommend treating incoming numeric strings as potentially unsafe; explicitly reject non-numeric types instead of coercing.
deploy-bot: started canary rollout quota-service@fix/strict-quota-parse at 09:30.
ops-bot: canary succeeded at 09:34, rolled to stable at 09:40.
Acme-SRE: acknowledging. We'll add a note to our runbook to avoid serializing floats as strings. Could Support add a short explanation to the customer about why a stringified small scale became zero?
Maria: yes, we'll prepare a short customer-facing blurb and attach logs + repro. We'll also open a postmortem and link engineering PR + deploy timeline. Short-term mitigation: enable the alert for effective_units==0 and add a runbook step to auto-notify Support channel. :white_check_mark:
